⛔ NOTHING ALLOCATES AN ID OF ANY KIND IN THIS LOOP, AND THE SAME COLLISION FIRED TWICE IN ONE HOUR ON TWO DIFFERENT ID SPACES — measured 2026-08-27, not hypothesised. ⭐ THE SECOND INSTANCE IS THE ONE THAT GENERALISES IT: this cycle and its sibling ALSO both filed ledger entries numbered AUT-PROP-009 and AUT-PROP-010, from the same max+1 derivation over the same committed ledger, for four entirely different items (RT-PARTNER-STRAT guards here, RT-ATR-ASSESS fixes there). Caught only by a rebase conflict on the ledger; the cycle-id half was caught only because the two claims raced on one push window. So the defect is not about cycle ids, it is about EVERY id the loop mints as max+1 from committed state — cycle ids, AUT-PROP entry ids, and anything later given the same treatment. This cycle derived 'CYC-0016' from the receipts directory; a sibling session that started ~50 s later derived the same id from the same committed state and committed c1bc934 'CYC-0016: claim AUT-010'. Both would have written research/autonomy/receipts/CYC-0016.json, and the ledger's `owner` field would have named one id for two different sessions on two different items. The collision was caught only because a rebase put the two claims side by side; had they not raced on the same push window, the second receipt would have silently overwritten the first. ⭐ THE DERIVATION IS THE BUG: every session computes the id from the same committed state, so concurrency is outside the derivation by construction, and the loop's own architecture assumes cycles are serial when nothing enforces that. Tiebreak taken here was ad-hoc — claimed first (04:20:40Z vs 04:21:20Z), landed second, so this cycle renumbered itself to CYC-0017 — and an ad-hoc tiebreak is not a mechanism. ⚠ FIX THE ALLOCATION, NOT THE TIEBREAK: an id that cannot collide (the session id, or a receipt filename carrying it) beats a rule about who yields, because the yielding session must first NOTICE, and a session that pushes cleanly never does. Check `health.py` too: `cycles_are_sized` reads receipts by session_id and would mis-group two sessions sharing a cycle id. ⛔⛔ THIRD INSTANCE, AND IT IS ALREADY IN THE COMMITTED LEDGER: `AUT-PD-012` IS USED TWICE, by two entirely different process defects — CYC-0011's 'the harness reported exit code 0 for a backgrounded preflight that FAILED' and CYC-0015's 'the ledger's retry budget governs nothing'. Those cycles were SEQUENTIAL, not concurrent, which kills the comfortable reading that this is a race: the derivation collides on its own. Present at 053a821 and on origin/main, so it predates CYC-0017 and has been sitting there unnoticed — nothing in the loop validates id uniqueness, so a duplicate is invisible until a human or a rebase trips over it. ⭐ THE FIX THEREFORE HAS TWO PARTS AND THE SECOND IS THE CHEAP ONE: allocate ids so they cannot collide, AND add a uniqueness assertion over `entries[*].id` to priority.py or the gate set, which would have caught all three instances at the commit that created them. De-duplicating the existing AUT-PD-012 pair belongs to this item.

entries.what: ⛔ THE FAN-OUT GOVERNANCE ROW READS A KEY NO RECEIPT WRITES — a one-word reader/writer mismatch that makes `fanout_is_governed` PERMANENTLY UNMEASURABLE, in the check CLAUDE.md §1 added precisely because 'the number governed nothing'. Measured 2026-08-27 by CYC-0017 against the live checker, not read off the docs: health.py's c_fanout_is_governed does `block.get('max_concurrent')`, while every receipt that has ever recorded a fan-out — CYC-0014, CYC-0016 and CYC-0017 as first written — stores the same value under `concurrent_max`. So the row reported DISPATCH-NOT-RECORDED and NAMED CYC-0014 and CYC-0017 as recording no `subagents` block when both plainly do. ⭐ AN INSTRUMENT REPORTING A FALSE ABSENCE IS THE FAILURE THIS REPOSITORY KEEPS PAYING FOR (CLAUDE.md §4), and this one wears the costume of the very restraint it cannot see: 'an absent record is not a record of restraint' is the correct principle printed over an incorrect reading. ⚠ NOT A DEFECT: the message lists five ids for six receipts — that is the reader's own `unrecorded[:5]` truncation, deliberate. ⛔ THE FIX IS NOT SIMPLY TO RENAME THE WRITERS. A receipt is immutable committed history (health.py's own comment says so and two conditions depend on it), so CYC-0014's and CYC-0016's fan-outs can never be made visible by editing them. Either the checker accepts BOTH spellings with the historical one documented as legacy, or the convention is pinned in one place that both the writer and the reader point at. CYC-0017's own receipt was corrected to `max_concurrent` at the time of filing, so the row has exactly one measurable cycle. ⭐ AND THE GENERAL FORM IS WORTH MORE THAN THE INSTANCE: a field name agreed in prose between a writer and a reader is not agreed at all — it is a hope, checked by nothing. Every other cross-file key this loop relies on has the same exposure, `handoff.child_session_id` included, which is why that one is spelled out verbatim in the handoff prompt. Sweep them.

⛔ 22 OF 32 PUBLICATION ENDPOINTS ARE READ BY NO INSTRUMENT AT ALL, AND EVERY CORRECTION ROUND MAKES IT WORSE. Measured 2026-08-27 by `python3 research/manuscripts/claim_coverage.py`: nr4a3-fusion-transcriptional-output.md 0/382, emc-surface-target-landscape.md 0/297, repurposing-hypotheses.md 0/216, emc-icdo-9231-classification.md 0/146, emc-atr-collaborator-package.md 0/144 — and nr4a3-degrader-paper.md 3/964, which is coverage in name only. ★ THE MECHANISM THIS ENTRY EXISTS FOR WAS MEASURED ON A REAL ROUND, NOT INFERRED: CYC-0011's round 4 on PUB-FUSION-PARTNER fixed nine defects and moved coverage 46/259 -> 50/271. The covered count did not move and the document grew twelve sentences, so the UNCOVERED surface ROSE 213 -> 221. Prose written to fix a defect is itself unwatched, so a hardening round without an instrumenting half enlarges exactly the surface `paper-hardening` §8a calls the remaining blocker risk. ⛔ THE WORK IS NOT 'INSTRUMENT EVERY ENDPOINT' — that is a list, and §8b.2's 33-mutation result says list-scoped fixes regress at the sibling nobody named. The work is a PREDICATE-scoped guard family plus the rule that a round which adds a sentence adds its guard in the same commit. ⭐ CYC-0013 ADDED THE MISSING HALF OF THE DIAGNOSIS, MEASURED ON ONE PAPER: the shortfall is not only that most endpoints have NO instrument, it is that an endpoint WITH one can still be unread, because the instrument's census pattern bounds what it can ever see. emc-fusion-partner-stratification.md scored 50/271 while its guard reported zero unbound figures, and 35 statistical quantities were outside both. ⛔ SO THE PREDICATE-SCOPED GUARD FAMILY THIS ENTRY ASKS FOR MUST BE AUDITED BY ITS PATTERN FIRST: ask what NOTATION a census cannot see before asking which documents it does not cover. The four notations CYC-0013 added (n = N, p-values in both printed forms, HR, cm/months) are reusable across every endpoint; nothing about them is specific to this paper.

⛔ `claim_coverage.py` CREDITS A TEST MODULE'S PATTERNS TO ANY DOCUMENT WHOSE BASENAME APPEARS ANYWHERE IN THAT MODULE — A COMMENT COUNTS. Measured 2026-08-27 (CYC-0014) while writing an unrelated guard: one declaration row cited the NR4A3 degrader manuscript by filename, and that single path made that paper read 85 of 964 sentences covered instead of 3 — 82 sentences of false coverage from a guard that opens no part of it. It was caught only by REGENERATING claim-coverage.json before committing; reading the diff of the test file could never have shown it. ⚠ THE FILE ALREADY DOCUMENTS THE FOOTGUN TWICE AND NOTHING TESTS IT, which is why it bit again. ⛔ AND THE OBVIOUS FIX IS REFUSED BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN BY TASTE: 'a module may only be credited for a document whose PATH it contains' is RED ON A CORRECT TREE. Measured the same day across research/manuscripts/tests: 42 module x document mentions, 18 path-like and 24 BASENAME-ONLY, nearly all of the 24 being ASO guards that do read their file through a shared helper. A widening is only a fix once it has been run. ★ SO THE WORK IS AN OBSERVED READ, NOT A SOURCE SCAN: credit a module for a document only when RUNNING it actually opens that file — instrument `open`/`io.open` under the module's own test run, or reuse claim_ablation's runner, which already RUNS guards rather than inferring them from source. ⚠ THIS MOVES EVERY COVERAGE NUMBER AND THEREFORE EVERY FLOOR, so it is NOT a small follow-on; the commit that lands it must say which floors moved and why, and must not lower one to go green. ⭐ IT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS AUT-COV-001 ONE LAYER UP: an instrument that reports on its own pattern, here the pattern being 'which module counts as a reader'.

⛔ THE HARNESS REPORTED 'exit code 0' FOR A BACKGROUNDED PREFLIGHT THAT FAILED. Measured 2026-08-27 (CYC-0011): `./scripts/preflight.sh > log 2>&1; echo "EXIT=$?" >> log` was backgrounded; the gate exited 1 on a stale archive manifest and printed `PREFLIGHT FAILED -- do not commit`, while the completion notification said exit code 0 — the wrapper's status, not the gate's. ⭐ THIS IS A SECOND, INDEPENDENT REASON FOR CLAUDE.md §6's 'wait on an ARTIFACT, not a process': the artifact marker was right and the status channel was not, and a session reading the notification alone commits on a red gate. The existing rule was written about `pgrep`/poll loops and reads as being about how to WAIT; this failure is about what to BELIEVE once the wait is over. Worth stating separately in the rule, and worth a preflight wrapper that writes its own verdict line the reader must consult.

⛔ THE LEDGER'S RETRY BUDGET GOVERNS NOTHING, AND THE CODE'S OWN COMMENT SAYS THAT IS THE FAILURE IT WAS MEANT TO PREVENT. Measured by CYC-0015 while deciding whether to take an item showing attempts=6 against retry_budget=3: (1) priority.py line ~177 hardcodes score_inputs['fruitless_attempts'] = 0 and computes it from nothing, though priority-weights.json defines a `fruitless_attempts` term; (2) `attempts` is incremented in exactly ONE place, release_stale_claims — i.e. it counts EXPIRED LEASES, not fruitless work; (3) NOTHING anywhere decrements `retry_budget` (grep: the only writers are priority.py's default of 3 and the modalities work_ledger, a different ledger); (4) health.py's queue_is_takeable filters on `retry_budget > 0` and reports a `retry_budget_spent` list that is therefore ALWAYS EMPTY. priority.py's own line-307 comment: 'so a route could be retried forever and the scorer's fruitless_attempts penalty could never fire.' It cannot fire. ⭐ THE FIX HAS A PROVEN MODEL IN THIS REPOSITORY: research/modalities/work_ledger.py implements the progress-aware version and TESTS it — Entry.fruitless_attempts() counts backwards and stops at the last evidence-fingerprint change, _apply_retry_budget blocks at MAX_FRUITLESS_ATTEMPTS, and progress wipes the count ('a dispatch that WORKED costs nothing'). Port that semantics; do not invent one. ⚠ AND RECORD THE HONEST READING SO THE FIX IS NOT OVERSOLD: a progress-aware counter would NOT have penalised AUT-PROP-002, which moved last_evidence_utc every cycle.
